parole.significato: poison hemlock, devil's bread, any extremely poisonous plant of the species Conium maculatum
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish بالدران (baldıran, “poison hemlock”), a Mongolic borrowing. parole.significato: antelope (any of several African mammals of the family Bovidae)
parole.testo: Borrowed from a Mongolic source, itself ultimately derived from Proto-Turkic *yegren. Cognate with Old Turkic 𐰘𐰏𐰼𐰤 (yegren, “reddish (of horses)”) and Azerbaijani ceyran.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish [Term?], from Old Anatolian Turkish طالو (ṭalu), of Mongolic origin. Compare Azerbaijani dal.
From Ottoman Turkish قارغاشه, قارغشه (kargaşa, “dispute; confusion; clamor of crows”), from Mongolic. Cognate with Kyrgyz каргаша (kargaşa, “disaster”).
From Ottoman Turkish قیلیبیق (kılıbık), probably from a Mongolic source. Compare Yakut килбик (kilbik, “timid, shy”), Mongolian гирби (girbi), etc.
From Ottoman Turkish نارین. From Mongolic. Compare Mongolian нарийн (nariin).

parole.significato: milch, used to produce milk or currently producing it for its offspring
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish صاغمال (sağmal, “milch”), a word that Nishanyan argues to be of Mongolic origin and related to Proto-Turkic *sag- (“to milk”). Cognate with Azerbaijani sağmal.
From Ottoman Turkish تاتار, from a Mongolic or Turkic name of a Khorezmian Turkic (Old Tatar) tribe.

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طولغه (tolga), variant of طوغلغه (toğulga, “helmet”), from a Mongolic source, ultimately from Proto-Mongolic *dugulga (“helmet”). From Ottoman Turkish اولوس (ulus), from a Mongolic source, compare Mongolian улс (uls, “state, country”), from Old Uyghur 𐽰𐽳𐾁𐽳𐽿 (uluš, “country, realm”) which is likely related to Old Uyghur 𐽰𐽳𐽶𐾁𐽰𐽿𐽹𐽰𐽷 (üleš-, “allot, to separate”), therefore from Proto-Turkic *üle- (“to divide, distribute, endow”).
